title: Mohenjo-daro (citadel mound and Great Bath)
summary: Mohenjo-daro, on the Indus in Sindh, Pakistan, was one of the largest cities of the Indus civilization, flourishing between about 2600 and 1900 BCE. Its western citadel mound, built up of mud-brick platforms and holding the Great Bath, a brick tank about 12 by 7 m, rose as much as 12 m above today's plain.

uncertainty.note: Harappa.com says the city flourished between 2600 and 1900 BCE, while UNESCO says the Indus civilization flourished between 2,500 and 1,500 BC. Start -2599 is 2600 BCE; the true start may lie later in the range. End is the present: the ruins survive.

phases.description: The city grew on mud-brick platforms and debris over the period 2600-1900 BCE; the sources opened do not date the citadel mound or Great Bath separately.

The city was abandoned after its flourishing period; a Buddhist stupa was built on the citadel over the ruins in the 2nd century AD (UNESCO). The start year is the end of the flourishing range, not a dated abandonment.

Britannica-type sources give 6 to 12 m for the citadel platform. Dates are the flourishing range, not the mound's construction.
